key_observations: Run terminated at 753 of 3000 planned iterations — the primary artifact; all metric values are early-training snapshots and conclusions are severely limited by Domain Rule 11 (no conclusions before 1000 iterations).

fell_over_rate=1.84 persists, but the per-iteration slope is negative (−0.0011/iter) and the final window ends at exactly the iteration-750 boundary where Domain Rule 2 says early spikes are still expected; the policy may have been self-correcting when stopped.

The shoulder-pitch hypothesis is falsified: reverting pose_std_walking_shoulder_pitch to 0.15 did not resolve instability, so the root cause is not that parameter alone or the prior three failures shared a different common factor.

gait_contact_cv_mean deteriorated from the 0.333 baseline to 0.568 — above the 0.4 irregular-gait threshold (Domain Rule 10); stance timing is worsening across experiments and was not addressed by this experiment's changes.

symmetry_vel_cost_mean=0.098 with symmetry_pos_cost_mean≈0.003 matches the mirror-pose-limp pattern from Domain Rule 9 — legs hold similar poses but move at different phases, which is a plausible driver of irregular contact CV.

gait_phase_regularity reward contribution is −1.479 and action_rate_l2 is −1.091; these two large competing penalties may be over-constraining the policy's ability to find stable locomotion, an interaction not addressed by the reverted parameters.
Exploration metrics are healthy for training age: entropy declining slowly (28.3→20.1) and action_std at 0.666 indicate no collapse; the policy is still exploring (Domain Rule 3 and 4).
landing_force_mean=40.5 N is comfortably within the 30–90 N healthy range; soft_landing weight does not need adjustment.
next_suggestion: Diagnose the truncation before changing any parameters: determine whether the run stopped at 753 iterations due to a technical failure (NaN, OOM, preemption) or an intentional early-stop criterion. If technical, rerun the identical config (air_time_weight=0.2, shoulder_pitch_std=0.15) to the full 3000 iterations — the declining fell_over slope means the policy may recover and the hypothesis cannot be evaluated on a 25%-complete run. If the run was genuinely complete, target the one metric that is consistently worsening across all failed runs: gait_contact_cv_mean. Make two changes: (1) increase limb_symmetry reward weight moderately (e.g. from its near-zero current contribution toward a value that actually penalises velocity asymmetry — the symmetry_vel_cost_mean=0.098 with near-zero pos_cost is the mirror-pose-limp diagnostic); (2) reduce the magnitude of gait_phase_regularity weight (e.g. toward −0.3 from its current strongly-negative value) to relieve reward competition with balance. Predicted side-effect to verify: limb_symmetry increase should reduce symmetry_vel_cost_mean and contact CV but may slightly reduce track_linear_velocity — if tracking does not drop, the result is suspect.
